suggestion.description: MAGPIE is ESA's first lunar rover, designed to operate for up to 10 Earth days at the lunar south pole, where it will drill into the subsurface to analyse material for water and other volatiles. The rover is being built by ispace Europe and is scheduled to launch with Intuitive Machines in 2029.
suggestion.landed_coords: illustrative south-pole site, kept clear of PROSPECT and LUPEX
suggestion.ou_involvement: The Open University is contracted to develop the Volatile Analyser (VA), a key element of the Lunar Volatiles Science (LVS) payload for ESA's MAGPIE rover. Building on the OU's heritage in ion-trap mass spectrometry, the instrument will analyse lunar material to identify and measure water and other volatiles, helping to characterise their abundance and how they vary with depth at the Moon's south pole.
